name: PRP for stretch marks
lead: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) for stretch marks involves processing a person's own blood to concentrate platelets and applying or injecting the product into stretch marks (striae distensae), often with microneedling or lasers. Proponents say the growth factors in platelets encourage collagen remodelling.

Wikipedia notes that stretch marks form from stretching of the dermis and that, according to a 2014 systematic review, no treatment has been clearly effective once they have formed; PRP is not discussed there [6].

Clinical research is limited to small registered trials, several of which combine PRP with another modality such as fractional lasers or fat grafting, making the effect of PRP alone hard to isolate. The registry records reviewed list no results [1][3][4][5].
infobox: Autologous blood-derived injection or topical application
Microneedling, fractional CO2 laser, fat grafting

paras: PRP is prepared from the patient's own blood, and sources describe it being used alone, with microneedling, or after laser treatment. Related products include platelet-rich fibrin (PRF), which a registered trial compares directly with PRP [1]. No preparation or administration details are given here.

NCT07561671, a 30-person trial started in February 2024 and listed as completed, compares PRP with PRF in striae distensae [1]. NCT07001644, a 50-person trial begun in 2022 with unknown status, compares microneedling with carboxytherapy in red stretch marks and appears in PRP-related searches rather than testing PRP itself [2].

Three small studies test combinations: nanofat grafting plus PRP versus microfat grafting plus PRP (12 participants, 2019) [3]; fractional laser plus PRP versus nanofat grafting plus PRP in striae gravidarum (10 participants, phase 3, 2017) [4]; and fractional carbon dioxide laser combined with PRP in striae gravidarum (16 participants, phase 3, completed) [5]. The registry records reviewed do not list outcomes, so no effect size is reported here.

PRP appears in skin and body-improvement discussions as an add-on to microneedling or laser treatment. No forum material was available for this entry, so community claims are not documented in detail.

timeline.event: Registration of a trial of fractional laser plus PRP versus nanofat plus PRP in striae gravidarum. [4]
Trials of nanofat or microfat grafting with PRP and of fractional CO2 laser with PRP begin. [3][5]
A PRP versus PRF trial in striae distensae begins. [1]

card.summary: Concentrated platelets from your own blood, tried on stretch marks mostly as an add-on in small trials.
card.note: Registered studies are small and mostly combine PRP with other treatments; no results were reviewed.

quick.overview:
PRP is made from a person's own blood and has been tried on stretch marks, usually together with microneedling, lasers or fat grafting.

The sources reviewed are a handful of small registered trials with no listed results, so its effect on stretch marks is not established here.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say platelet growth factors stimulate collagen and tissue repair in the skin.
quick.risks: The sources reviewed give no safety data. As a blood-derived injectable procedure, it is performed by clinicians.
